messages.text: you were going to compare the different miner models i was looking at, but i accidentally closed the tab. would you run the comparison now?

Quick version: the BS-4 is $599.99 for 18 TH/s, ships October 31. The B30 is $899 for about 30 TH/s — more hashrate per dollar, ships November 30.

What do you pay per kWh? I'll run sats and power cost on both.

Here they are at 24¢:

BS-4, 18 TH/s at ~300 W — about $52 a month in power. $599.99, ships October 31, 2026.

B30, 30 TH/s at 485 W in Turbo — about $84 a month. It also has Balanced (24 TH/s, 350 W, ~$60) and ECO (18 TH/s, 230 W, ~$40), so at the BS-4's hashrate it uses a third less power. $899, ships November 30, 2026.

At 24¢ that ECO mode is the real argument: same 18 TH/s as the BS-4 for ~$12 less a month, and you can turn it up when you want the bigger block shot. I'd take the B30.

Both draw for a full block every ten minutes, year after year, and stack sats to your own wallet meanwhile. Want me to build the B30 cart?
Can the B30 be clocked even lower?

The published modes stop at ECO: 18 TH/s at 230 W, 12.8 J/TH. That's the lowest setting Harlo documents.

Whether the firmware lets you dial a custom clock below that, I won't guess. Want me to put that question to JD, who handles the hardware? He'd confirm by email.

JD has it. The team's in at 10am ET today and the answer comes to your email.

One thing while we wait: do you want me to build the B30 cart now, or hold until you hear on the low-clock question?
please also let me know if the B30's asics can be individually brought offline and back online without turning off the miner.
